record.title: A paper shows policy shifts can invalidate one-step world-model coverage, then tests ratio-weighted recalibration
record.summary: The Aug 20, 2026 preprint studies uncertainty calibration when a fixed robot world model is evaluated under a changed action-selection policy. Under a shared conditional transition mechanism, it derives a density-ratio correction for transporting one-step marginal conformal coverage and a bound linking estimated-ratio error to coverage loss. In an author-run experiment using 192 physical Franka transitions from 15 episodes, the predictor remains fixed while the evaluation pool is reweighted by an outcome-blind action-magnitude statistic. At nominal 90% coverage and the strongest controlled shift, ordinary source calibration covers 55.0%; oracle and learned ratio weighting cover 91.0% and 90.9%. The study is paper-reported and does not test a new live policy rollout: the target distribution is a controlled reweighting of the same finite pool. Its guarantees require shared conditional dynamics and are one-step and marginal, not joint trajectory guarantees.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors derive a one-step marginal weighted-conformal coverage result for a fixed predictor when source and target share the conditional outcome mechanism and the target query distribution is absolutely continuous with respect to the source; for policy-controlled dynamics the density ratio factors into state-occupancy and action-propensity terms.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 192 one-step physical Franka transitions from 15 episodes, under the strongest controlled reweighting of the same pool, nominal 90% coverage is 55.0% with ordinary source calibration, 91.0% with oracle ratio weighting and 90.9% with learned ratio weighting; the predictor is held fixed.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported experiment does not establish calibration during a live deployment-policy change, under changed transition mechanisms, or for joint multi-step trajectory coverage; it uses controlled distribution tilts on one fixed finite pool and reports no independent reproduction.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported formal and empirical findings have not been independently reproduced in this review.
The physical experiment reweights one fixed pool; it does not evaluate observations collected after a planner actually changes its policy or state occupancy.
The guarantee is one-step and marginal under shared conditional dynamics; mechanism shift and joint trajectory coverage are outside the paper’s stated scope.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, a method that tracks deployment-policy shifts in one-step world-model uncertainty could change how robotics teams set prediction-set coverage without retraining a fixed predictor. The paper reports a sharp controlled failure and recalibration on a small physical Franka transition pool; it does not establish performance under live policy changes, mechanism shifts or multi-step deployment.
limitations: Author-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed in this review.

The physical evaluation uses 192 one-step transitions from 15 Franka episodes covering folding, picking and pushing; the target law is a controlled reweighting of this fixed pool, not a live policy rollout.
The guarantee is one-step and marginal and assumes shared conditional dynamics, target support contained in source support and pre-outcome weights.
Mechanism shift, including generated dynamics, and joint trajectory coverage are explicitly left for additional methods or data.

At the strongest shift, learned weighting restores reported coverage but effective sample size falls from 500 to 73 and the conformal radius widens; clipping at five raises effective sample size to 125 but lowers coverage to 83.8% by changing the target surrogate.
brief.summary: The Aug 20, 2026 preprint studies uncertainty calibration when a fixed robot world model is evaluated under a changed action-selection policy. Under a shared conditional transition mechanism, it derives a density-ratio correction for transporting one-step marginal conformal coverage and a bound linking estimated-ratio error to coverage loss. In an author-run experiment using 192 physical Franka transitions from 15 episodes, the predictor remains fixed while the evaluation pool is reweighted by an outcome-blind action-magnitude statistic. At nominal 90% coverage and the strongest controlled shift, ordinary source calibration covers 55.0%; oracle and learned ratio weighting cover 91.0% and 90.9%. The study is paper-reported and does not test a new live policy rollout: the target distribution is a controlled reweighting of the same finite pool. technical.claimed_result: Weighted conformal calibration can target a changed query distribution for a fixed one-step predictor when the outcome mechanism is shared; estimated source/target density ratios give a coverage penalty tied to surrogate mismatch. In the reported fixed-pool test, learned weighting closely tracks oracle weighting.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary preprint documents its mathematical argument, protocol and author-reported results. This review inspected the paper but did not reproduce its proof, code or experiments.
technical.implementation_status: Research result in a preprint; no deployed calibration system or live policy-shift trial was evaluated.
technical.mechanism: For policy-controlled dynamics, the target/source density ratio is the product of a state-occupancy ratio and an action-propensity ratio. A source-versus-target domain classifier estimates the ratio from pre-outcome covariates; weighted conformal quantiles then recalibrate the fixed predictor for the target query law.
technical.regime: One-step latent prediction using a released DINO-WM predictor on 192 physical Franka transitions from 15 episodes. Controlled target laws reweight the observed pool by a preregistered, outcome-blind translational action-magnitude statistic. The strongest shift has total variation 63.7%; calibration draws use 500 source transitions with replacement and evaluation draws use 10,000 pool samples, repeated 50 times.
technical.reproducibility: Paper provides a Lean 4 formalization and names the released JEPA-WMs implementation and physical evaluation data. This review did not independently run the Lean project or empirical protocol.
technical.strongest_baseline: Ordinary conformal calibration on the source distribution, compared with oracle and learned-ratio weighting while holding the predictor and transition pool fixed.

brief.title: A paper shows policy shifts can invalidate one-step world-model coverage, then tests ratio-weighted recalibration
brief.why_it_matters: A world model can keep the same predictor while a planner changes which state-action inputs it queries. If the query distribution shifts, coverage calibrated on the data-collection policy may cease to apply. This paper gives a concrete correction and a controlled physical-data example; the bounded result motivates policy-aware uncertainty checks but does not establish them for live deployment or changing dynamics.
